transcript.text: I've just bought an AEG L7FEE865R and the Eco 40-60 wash says 3:39 and seems to take forever. My old machine did a 40 wash in an hour. Is it faulty? Should I send it back?

No, your washing machine is not faulty, and you should not send it back. The Eco 40-60 program taking approximately 3 hours and 39 minutes is completely normal for this model (and most modern AEG/Indesit group machines).

Here’s why:

### 1. How the Eco 40-60 Program Works
The "Eco" programs are designed to be energy-efficient, not fast. They achieve lower energy and water consumption by:
• Using less hot water (heating water is the most energy-intensive part of a wash).
• Extending the wash time significantly to compensate for the lower temperature and reduced mechanical action.
• Soaking and rinsing more thoroughly over a longer period.

The "40-60" in the name means it can effectively clean clothes washed at 40°C or even up to 60°C, but it does so using a gentle, long-duration process. This is why it takes ~3.5 hours instead of 1 hour.

### 2. Comparison with Your Old Machine
Your old machine likely had a shorter, more aggressive wash cycle that used more water and heated it quickly. While faster, these older-style cycles are generally less energy-efficient and can be harsher on fabrics. The Eco program is certified by EU energy labels to use significantly less electricity and water per year than standard quick programs.

### 3. What You Can Do If Time Is a Concern
If you need clothes washed quickly:
• Use a different cycle: Select "Quick Wash," "15' or 30' Wash," or "Cottons" at 40°C or 60°C. These will be much faster (often 30–60 minutes) but will use more energy and water.
• Use the "SpeedPerfect" feature: Many AEG models have a button called SpeedPerfect (or similar). Pressing this adds extra heat and agitation to reduce wash time while maintaining cleaning performance, though it will slightly increase energy use.

### 4. When to Be Concerned
The only reason to suspect a fault is if:
• The machine stops mid-cycle or displays an error code.
• It takes significantly longer than stated (e.g., over 5 hours) for the Eco program.
• Clothes are not coming out clean despite using the correct settings and detergent.

### Recommendation
Your AEG L7FEE865R is working as designed. The Eco 40-60 program is ideal for:
• Daily loads of moderately soiled clothes.
• Saving money on energy bills over time.
• Being gentler on fabrics due to lower temperatures and longer, softer agitation.

Tip: For best results with the Eco program, use liquid detergent (not powder) and ensure you’re not overloading the machine. The longer soak time works best when clothes have enough room to move freely.

Enjoy your new washer! It’s a high-quality machine that will save you money on utilities in the long run, even if it takes longer per cycle.
Ok, thanks, that's reassuring. The assistant mentioned a SpeedPerfect button but mine doesn't seem to have that, there's a TimeManager button though. Would that shorten it?

Yes, the TimeManager button is AEG’s equivalent of the "SpeedPerfect" feature on other brands. It will definitely help shorten the cycle time.

Here’s how it works:

### What TimeManager Does
• When you select a program (like Eco 40-60), pressing the TimeManager button allows you to manually reduce the wash duration.
• The display will show options like "1h," "2h," or similar, depending on the base program. You can choose a shorter time that suits your needs.

### Important Trade-offs
While TimeManager is convenient for saving time, keep in mind:
• Energy Use Increases: Shortening the cycle means the machine may need to use more water and heat it more aggressively to compensate for the reduced wash time. This will increase electricity and water consumption compared to the standard Eco program.
• Cleaning Performance May Vary: For heavily soiled clothes, a shortened Eco cycle might not clean as effectively as the full duration. However, for normal loads, it should still provide good results.

### Recommendation
• If you’re in a hurry and have a normal load of laundry, use TimeManager to reduce the cycle to 1–2 hours. This will be much faster than the default 3:39 Eco time.
• If you want maximum energy efficiency (e.g., for lightly soiled clothes or when running off solar power), stick with the full Eco 40-60 cycle.

You can experiment with different TimeManager settings to find a balance between speed and cleaning performance that works best for your household.
